translations.idiomatic: On yimao the capital was shaken by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊申，東魏人來聘，遣兼散騎常侍明少遐報聘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on wushen, men of Eastern Wei came on a friendly mission; Acting Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Ming Shaoxia was sent on a return mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer envoys from Eastern Wei arrived on a friendly mission; Acting Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Ming Shaoxia was sent on a return mission.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月丙子，詔停所在使役女丁。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter on bingzi, an edict halted corvée by women wherever it was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on bingzi, an edict halted corvée by women wherever it was imposed.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬寅，東魏人來聘，遣兼散騎常侍袁狎報聘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on renyin, men of Eastern Wei came on a friendly mission; Acting Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Xia was sent on a return mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month envoys from Eastern Wei arrived on a friendly mission; Acting Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Xia was sent on a return mission.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，于宮城西立士林館，延集學者。

translations.literal: On bingchen, west of the palace the Forest of Scholars Hall was established to gather scholars.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the Forest of Scholars Hall was established west of the palace to gather scholars.

sentences.zh: 是歲，宕昌、蠕蠕、高麗、百濟、滑國各遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: This year, Dangchang, Rouran, Goguryeo, Baekje, and Huaxia each sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Dangchang, Rouran, Goguryeo, Baekje, and Huaxia each sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 百濟求涅盤等經疏及醫工、畫師、毛詩博士，並許之。

translations.literal: Baekje requested Nirvana and other sutra commentaries and medical artisans, painters, and a Filial Piety Classic doctor — all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje requested Nirvana and other sutra commentaries, medical artisans, painters, and a Filial Piety Classic doctor — all were granted.

sentences.zh: 交州人李賁攻刺史蕭諮。

translations.literal: Li Ben of Jiaozhou attacked Governor Xiao Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ben of Jiaozhou attacked Governor Xiao Zi.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月，安成郡人劉敬躬挾左道以反。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the eighth year, Liu Jinggong of Ancheng Commandery relied on heterodox ways to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the eighth year Liu Jinggong of Ancheng Commandery relied on heterodox ways to rebel.

sentences.zh: 二月戊戌，江州刺史湘東王繹遣中兵曹子郢討禽之，送於都，斬之建康市。

translations.literal: In the second month on wuxu, Prince of Xiangdong Yi, Governor of Jiang Province, dispatched Central Army Cao Ziying to suppress and capture him; he was sent to the capital and executed in the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuxu, Prince of Xiangdong Yi, Governor of Jiang Province, dispatched Central Army Cao Ziying to suppress and capture him; he was sent to the capital and executed in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 三月，于江州新蔡高塘立頌平屯，墾作蠻田。

translations.literal: In the third month, at Gaotang in Xincai of Jiang Province the Songping garrison was established to reclaim barbarian fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Songping garrison was established at Gaotang in Xincai of Jiang Province to reclaim barbarian fields.

sentences.zh: 九年春閏正月丙申，地震，生毛。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of spring of the ninth year on bingshen, an earthquake; hair grew.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of spring of the ninth year, on bingshen, an earthquake struck and hair grew from the ground.

sentences.zh: 三月，以太子詹事謝舉為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the third month, Xie Ju, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xie Ju, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，林邑王破德州，攻李賁，賁將范修又破林邑王於九德，敗走之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, the King of Linyi broke Dezhou and attacked Li Ben; Ben's general Fan Xiu again defeated the King of Linyi at Jiude and drove him off in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the King of Linyi broke Dezhou and attacked Li Ben; Ben's general Fan Xiu again defeated the King of Linyi at Jiude and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，益州刺史武陵王紀進號征西將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, Prince of Yiling Ji, Governor of Yizhou, was promoted to General Who Conquers the West with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Prince of Yiling Ji, Governor of Yizhou, was promoted to General Who Conquers the West with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月，李賁竊號於交址，年號天德。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the tenth year, Li Ben usurped an era name at Jiaozhi — Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the tenth year Li Ben usurped an era name at Jiaozhi — Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 三月甲午，幸蘭陵。

translations.literal: In the third month on jiawu, the Emperor visited Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu, the Emperor visited Lanling.

sentences.zh: 庚子，謁建陵，有紫雲蔭陵上，食頃乃散。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he visited Jiancheng; purple clouds shaded the tomb for the time of a meal before dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he visited Jiancheng; purple clouds shaded the tomb for the time of a meal before dispersing.

sentences.zh: 帝望陵流涕，所沾草皆變色，陵傍有枯泉，至是而流水香潔。

translations.literal: The Emperor gazed at the tomb and wept; wherever his tears fell the grass changed color; beside the tomb was a dry spring that now flowed with fragrant, pure water.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gazed at the tomb and wept; wherever his tears fell the grass changed color; beside the tomb a dry spring now flowed with fragrant, pure water.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，哭于修陵。

translations.literal: On xinchou, he wept at Xiuling.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he wept at Xiuling.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，於皇基寺設法會，詔賜蘭陵老少位一階，並加頒賚。

translations.literal: On renyin, at Huangji Temple a dharma assembly was set up; an edict granted one rank to the old and young of Lanling and added distributions.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin a dharma assembly was set up at Huangji Temple; an edict granted one rank to the old and young of Lanling and added distributions.

sentences.zh: 所經縣邑，無出今年租賦。

translations.literal: The counties and townships passed through were exempted from this year's land tax and levies.
translations.idiomatic: The counties and townships he passed through were exempted from this year's land tax and levies.

sentences.zh: 因賦還舊鄉詩。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed a poem on returning to his old home.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he composed a poem on returning to his old home.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，詔園陵職司，恭事勤勞，並錫位一階，並加賜賚。

translations.literal: On guimao, an edict: the officials of the imperial tombs, reverent in service and diligent in labor, were all granted one rank and additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao an edict granted one rank and additional gifts to the officials of the imperial tombs for reverent service and diligent labor.

sentences.zh: 己酉，幸京口城北固樓，因改名北顧。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the Emperor visited the Beigu Tower north of Jingkou and thereupon renamed it Beigu — "Northward Gaze."
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the Emperor visited the Beigu Tower north of Jingkou and renamed it Beigu — "Northward Gaze."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，幸回賓亭，宴帝鄉故老及所經近縣奉迎候者少長數千人，各賚錢二千。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Emperor visited the Huibin Pavilion and feasted the old men of the imperial homeland and those from nearby counties who came to welcome him — young and old numbering several thousand — each granted two thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Emperor visited the Huibin Pavilion and feasted the old men of the imperial homeland and those from nearby counties who came to welcome him — several thousand young and old — each receiving two thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，至自蘭陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on yimao, he returned from Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on yimao, he returned from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 詔鰥寡孤獨尤貧者，贍恤各有差。

translations.literal: An edict: widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary, and those especially poor, received relief according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted relief according to rank to widowers, widows, orphans, the solitary, and those especially poor.

sentences.zh: 五月，廣州人盧子略反，刺史新渝侯映討平之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Lu Zilue of Guangzhou rebelled; Governor Prince of Xinyu Ying suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Lu Zilue of Guangzhou rebelled; Governor Prince of Xinyu Ying suppressed and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 詔曲赦廣州。

translations.literal: An edict granted a partial amnesty for Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted a partial amnesty for Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋九月己丑，赦。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn on jichou, a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, on jichou, a pardon was declared.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，大雪，平地三尺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, heavy snow; three feet on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter heavy snow piled three feet deep on level ground.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月，震華林園光嚴殿、重雲閣。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the eleventh year, the Hall of Radiant Solemnity and the Chongyun Pavilion in the Hualin Garden shook.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the eleventh year the Hall of Radiant Solemnity and the Chongyun Pavilion in the Hualin Garden were shaken.

sentences.zh: 帝自貶拜謝上天，累刻乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself demoted himself and bowed in apology to Heaven; for many quarters of an hour before it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor demoted himself and bowed in apology to Heaven; for many quarters of an hour before the tremors stopped.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，東魏人來聘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, men of Eastern Wei came on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer envoys from Eastern Wei arrived on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己未，詔復開贖罪典。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on jiwei, an edict restored the statute for ransoming offenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiwei, an edict restored the statute for ransoming offenses.

sentences.zh: 中大同元年春正月丁未，曲阿縣建陵隧口石辟邪起舞，有大蛇鬥隧中，其一被傷奔走。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Zhongdatong on dingwei, at the Jiancheng tomb entrance in Qu'e County the stone ward-off-evil danced; a great serpent fought in the tunnel, one wounded and fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the first year of Zhongdatong, on dingwei, at the Jiancheng tomb entrance in Qu'e County the stone ward-off-evil danced; a great serpent fought in the tunnel and one was wounded and fled.

sentences.zh: 青蟲食陵樹葉略盡。

translations.literal: Green worms ate the tomb trees' leaves nearly clean.
translations.idiomatic: Green worms ate the tomb trees' leaves nearly bare.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，交州刺史楊膘克交址嘉甯城，李賁竄入屈獠洞。

translations.literal: On guichou, Yang Biao, Governor of Jiaozhou, captured Jianing city in Jiaozhi; Li Ben fled into the Qu Liao cave.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Yang Biao, Governor of Jiaozhou, captured Jianing city in Jiaozhi; Li Ben fled into the Qu Liao cave.

sentences.zh: 交州平。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 三月乙巳，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month on yisi, a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yisi, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，幸同泰寺講金字三慧經，仍施身。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Emperor visited Tongtai Temple to expound the gold-letter Three Wisdom Sutra, and again offered his body.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Emperor visited Tongtai Temple to expound the gold-letter Three Wisdom Sutra and again offered his body to the sangha.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙戌，皇太子以下奉贖，仍於同泰寺解講，設法會，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on bingxu, the Crown Prince and those below offered ransom; still at Tongtai Temple the lecture was concluded and a dharma assembly set up; a great amnesty; the era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on bingxu, the Crown Prince and those below offered ransom; at Tongtai Temple the lecture was concluded and a dharma assembly convened; a general amnesty was declared and the reign era changed.

sentences.zh: 是夜，同泰寺災。

translations.literal: That night, Tongtai Temple was destroyed by fire.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tongtai Temple was destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: 六月辛巳，竟天有聲，如風水相薄。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on xinsi, sound filled the sky like wind and water beating against each other.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi, sound filled the sky like wind and water beating against each other.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲子，詔自今有犯罪者，非大逆，父母祖父母勿坐。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on jiazi, an edict: from now on for those who commit crimes, except great treason, parents and grandparents were not to be implicated.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiazi, an edict ordered that from then on, except for great treason, parents and grandparents were not to be implicated when someone committed a crime.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「朝四暮三，眾狙皆喜，名實未虧，而喜怒為用。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict said: "Morning four, evening three — all the monkeys rejoice; name and reality are not diminished, yet joy and anger are made use of.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin an edict declared: "Morning four, evening three — all the monkeys rejoice; name and reality are unchanged, yet joy and anger are manipulated.

sentences.zh: 頃聞外間多用九佰錢，佰減則物貴，佰足則物賤，非物有貴賤，是心有顛倒。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that outside mostly use nine-hundred cash; when the hundred is reduced goods are dear, when the hundred is full goods are cheap — it is not that goods have dearth and plenty, but that the heart has inversion.
translations.idiomatic: Recently it is heard that outside mostly use nine-hundred cash; when the hundred is shaved goods grow dear, when the hundred is full goods grow cheap — it is not that goods have dearth and plenty, but that minds are turned upside down.

sentences.zh: 至於遠方，日更滋甚。

translations.literal: As for distant regions, day by day it grows worse.
translations.idiomatic: In distant regions the abuse grows worse day by day.

sentences.zh: 自今可通用足佰錢。

translations.literal: From now on full hundred cash may be used universally.
translations.idiomatic: From now on full hundred cash shall be used everywhere.

sentences.zh: 」八月丁丑，東揚州刺史武昌王謷薨。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month on dingchou, Prince of Wuchang Ao, Governor of Eastern Yang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingchou, Prince of Wuchang Ao, Governor of Eastern Yang, died.

sentences.zh: 甲午，渴盤陀國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Kapisa sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Kapisa sent envoys presenting local products.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸酉，汝陰王劉哲薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on guiyou, Prince of Ruyin Liu Zhe died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on guiyou, Prince of Ruyin Liu Zhe died.

sentences.zh: 太清元年春正月己亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Taiqing on jihai, the first day of the month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Taiqing, on jihai, the first day of the first month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，荊州刺史廬陵王續薨。

translations.literal: On renyin, Prince of Luling Xu, Governor of Jing Province, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Prince of Luling Xu, Governor of Jing Province, died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the southern suburb was sacrificed to; a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the court sacrificed at the southern suburb and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 甲子，祀明堂。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Bright Hall was sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the court sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 是月，東魏相勃海王高歡薨。

translations.literal: This month, Chancellor Prince of Bohai Gao Huan of Eastern Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: That month Chancellor Prince of Bohai Gao Huan of Eastern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 二月己卯，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: In the second month on jimao, a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jimao, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，東魏司徒侯景求以河南十三州內屬。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Hou Jing, Minister of Works of Eastern Wei, requested to submit the thirteen provinces of Henan to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Hou Jing, Minister of Works of Eastern Wei, requested to submit the thirteen provinces of Henan to Liang.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以景為大將軍，封河南王，大行台，承制如鄧禹故事。

translations.literal: On renwu, Jing was made Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Henan, given the Great Mobile Office, and empowered to act on imperial authority after the precedent of Deng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Jing was appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Henan, given the Great Mobile Office, and empowered to act on imperial authority after the precedent of Deng Yu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，耕藉田。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the ceremonial field was plowed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the ceremonial field was plowed.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，幸同泰寺，設無遮大會。

translations.literal: In the third month on gengzi, the Emperor visited Tongtai Temple and set up the Unrestricted Great Assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengzi, the Emperor visited Tongtai Temple and convened the Unrestricted Great Assembly.

sentences.zh: 上釋御服，服法衣，行清淨大舍，名曰：「羯磨」。

translations.literal: The sovereign cast off imperial robes, wore dharma robes, and undertook the great pure offering, named "Karma Repentance."
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign cast off imperial robes and wore dharma robes, undertaking the great pure offering named Karma Repentance.

sentences.zh: 以五明殿為房，設素木床、葛帳、土瓦器，乘小輿，私人執役。

translations.literal: The Hall of Five Brightnesses was made his room; a plain wooden bed, hemp curtain, and earthenware vessels were set; he rode a small palanquin; private persons performed service.
translations.idiomatic: He made the Hall of Five Brightnesses his room, with a plain wooden bed, hemp curtain, and earthenware vessels, riding a small palanquin while private persons served him.

sentences.zh: 乘輿法服，一皆屏除。

translations.literal: Imperial carriage and ritual robes were all removed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial carriage and ritual robes were all set aside.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遣司州刺史羊鴉仁率土州刺史桓和、仁州刺史湛海珍等應接侯景。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Yang Yaren, Governor of Si Province, was dispatched to lead Huan He, Governor of Tu Province, Zhan Haizhen, Governor of Ren Province, and others to support Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Yang Yaren, Governor of Si Province, was dispatched to lead Huan He, Governor of Tu Province, Zhan Haizhen, Governor of Ren Province, and others to support Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 兵未至，而東魏遣兵攻景，景又割地求救于西魏，方解圍。

translations.literal: Before the troops arrived, Eastern Wei dispatched troops to attack Jing; Jing also ceded territory to beg rescue from Western Wei, and only then was the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Before the troops arrived Eastern Wei dispatched troops to attack Jing; Jing also ceded territory to beg rescue from Western Wei, and only then was the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝升光嚴殿講堂，坐師子座，講金字三慧經，捨身。

translations.literal: On yisi, the Emperor ascended the lecture hall of the Hall of Radiant Solemnity, sat on the lion seat, expounded the gold-letter Three Wisdom Sutra, and offered his body.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Emperor ascended the lecture hall of the Hall of Radiant Solemnity, sat on the lion seat, expounded the gold-letter Three Wisdom Sutra, and offered his body.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚午，群臣以錢一億萬奉贖皇帝菩薩，僧眾默許。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on gengwu, the ministers with one hundred million in cash offered to ransom the Emperor bodhisattva; the monastic assembly silently assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on gengwu, the ministers offered one hundred million in cash to ransom the Emperor bodhisattva; the monastic assembly silently assented.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，百辟詣鳳莊門奉表，三請三答，頓首，並如中大通元年故事。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the hundred ministers went to the Fengzhuang Gate with a memorial; three requests and three answers, prostrations — all as in the precedent of the first year of Zhongdatong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the hundred ministers went to the Fengzhuang Gate with a memorial; three requests and three answers with prostrations — all as in the precedent of the first year of Zhongdatong.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，服袞冕。

translations.literal: On dinghai, he donned the robe and cap of state.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he donned the robe and cap of state.

sentences.zh: 禦輦還宮。

translations.literal: He rode the imperial carriage back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rode the imperial carriage back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 幸太極殿，如即位禮，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: He visited the Hall of Supreme Polarity; as at the accession rites; a great amnesty; the era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the Hall of Supreme Polarity as at the accession rites, declared a general amnesty, and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 是月，神馬出，皇太子獻寶馬頌。

translations.literal: This month, a divine horse appeared; the Crown Prince presented an ode on the treasured horse.
translations.idiomatic: That month a divine horse appeared; the Crown Prince presented an ode on the treasured horse.

sentences.zh: 六月戊辰，以前雍州刺史鄱陽王範為征北將軍，總督漢北征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on wuchen, Prince of Poyang Fan, former Governor of Yong Province, was made General Who Conquers the North and overall commander of the Hanbei campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuchen, Prince of Poyang Fan, former Governor of Yong Province, was appointed General Who Conquers the North and overall commander of the Hanbei campaigns.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚申，羊鴉仁入縣瓠城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on gengshen, Yang Yaren entered Xuanhu city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on gengshen, Yang Yaren entered Xuanhu city.

sentences.zh: 八月乙丑，諸軍北征，以南豫州刺史蕭明為大都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on yichou, the armies marched north; Xiao Ming, Governor of Southern Yu Province, was made Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yichou, the armies marched north; Xiao Ming, Governor of Southern Yu Province, was appointed Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 赦緣邊初附諸州。

translations.literal: A pardon for the border provinces newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A pardon was declared for the border provinces newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以大將軍侯景錄行台尚書事。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Grand General Hou Jing was put in charge of the Mobile Office Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Grand General Hou Jing was put in charge of Mobile Office Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 九月癸卯，王游苑成，輿駕幸苑。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on guimao, the Wangyou Park was completed; the imperial carriage visited the park.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guimao, the Wangyou Park was completed and the imperial carriage visited the park.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，東魏將慕容紹宗大敗蕭明於寒山，明被俘執。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, Murong Shaozong of Eastern Wei greatly defeated Xiao Ming at Hanshan; Ming was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Murong Shaozong of Eastern Wei greatly defeated Xiao Ming at Hanshan and captured him alive.

sentences.zh: 紹宗進圍潼州。

translations.literal: Shaozong advanced to besiege Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong advanced to besiege Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊辰，命太子舍人元貞還北為東魏主。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on wuchen, Attendant of the Crown Prince Yuan Zhen was ordered back north to serve as ruler of Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuchen, Attendant of the Crown Prince Yuan Zhen was ordered back north to serve as ruler of Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月癸巳朔，兩月相承如鉤，見於西方。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year on guisi, the first day of the month, two moons followed each other like hooks, appearing in the west.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year, on guisi, the first day of the first month, two moons followed each other like hooks, appearing in the west.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔在位各舉所知。

translations.literal: On wuxu, an edict ordered those in office each to recommend those they knew.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu an edict ordered those in office each to recommend those they knew.

sentences.zh: 己亥，東魏克渦陽。

translations.literal: On jihai, Eastern Wei captured Guoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Eastern Wei captured Guoyang.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以尚書僕射謝舉為尚書令，以守吏部尚書王克為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Xie Ju, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat; Wang Ke, Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Xie Ju, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Director of the Secretariat; Wang Ke, Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，東魏克殷、豫二州。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Eastern Wei captured Yin and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Eastern Wei captured Yin and Yu provinces.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，撫東將軍高麗王高延卒，以其子成為甯東將軍、高麗王、樂浪公。

translations.literal: In the third month on jiachen, Gao Yan, King of Goguryeo and General Who Pacifies the East, died; his son Cheng was made General Who Pacifies the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiachen, Gao Yan, King of Goguryeo and General Who Pacifies the East, died; his son Cheng was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 己未，屈獠洞斬李賁，傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the Qu Liao cave beheaded Li Ben and sent the head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the Qu Liao cave beheaded Li Ben and sent the head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙子，詔在朝及州郡各舉士。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on bingzi, an edict ordered those at court and in the provinces and commanderies each to recommend scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on bingzi, an edict ordered those at court and in the provinces and commanderies each to recommend scholars.

sentences.zh: 五月辛丑，以新除中書令邵陵王綸為安前將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on xinchou, the newly appointed Director of the Secretariat Prince of Shaoling Lun was made General Who Stabilizes the Front with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinchou, the newly appointed Director of the Secretariat Prince of Shaoling Lun was made General Who Stabilizes the Front with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，曲赦交、愛、德三州。

translations.literal: On xinhai, a partial amnesty for the three provinces of Jiao, Ai, and De.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai a partial amnesty was declared for Jiao, Ai, and De provinces.

sentences.zh: 六月，天裂於西北，長十丈，闊二丈，光出如電，其聲若雷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the sky split in the northwest — ten zhang long, two zhang wide; light issued like lightning; the sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the sky split in the northwest — ten zhang long and two zhang wide; light issued like lightning and the sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，使兼散騎常侍謝班聘於東魏結和。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Acting Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Ban was sent on a friendly mission to Eastern Wei to conclude peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Acting Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Ban was sent on a friendly mission to Eastern Wei to conclude peace.

sentences.zh: 八月戊戌，侯景舉兵反。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on wuxu, Hou Jing raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuxu, Hou Jing raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，使開府儀同三司邵陵王綸都督眾軍討景，曲赦南豫州。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Prince of Shaoling Lun, with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies, was made Commander-in-Chief to suppress Jing; a partial amnesty for Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Prince of Shaoling Lun, with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies, was appointed commander-in-chief to suppress Jing; a partial amnesty was declared for Southern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 九月戊辰，地震，江左尤甚，壞屋殺人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on wuchen, an earthquake; east of the river especially severe; buildings collapsed and people were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuchen, an earthquake struck; east of the river the damage was especially severe — buildings collapsed and people were killed.

sentences.zh: 地生白毛，長二尺。

translations.literal: From the ground white hair grew, two chi long.
translations.idiomatic: White hair grew from the ground, two chi long.

sentences.zh: 益州市有飛蜂萬群，螫人死。

translations.literal: In Yizhou there were swarms of flying bees numbering ten thousand; stings killed people.
translations.idiomatic: In Yizhou swarms of flying bees numbering in the tens of thousands stung people to death.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，侯景襲譙州，進攻陷曆陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Hou Jing raided Qiao Province and advanced to attack and capture Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Hou Jing raided Qiao Province and advanced to attack and capture Liyang.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以臨賀王正德為平北將軍，都督諸軍屯丹陽郡。

translations.literal: On wushen, Prince of Linhe Zhengde was made General Who Pacifies the North and commander of the armies garrisoned in Danyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Prince of Linhe Zhengde was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and commander of the armies garrisoned in Danyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 己酉，景自橫江濟採石。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Jing crossed the Yangtze from Hengjiang at Caishiji.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Jing crossed the Yangtze from Hengjiang at Caishiji.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，至建鄴，臨賀王正德率眾附賊。

translations.literal: On xinhai, he reached Jiankang; Prince of Linhe Zhengde led his forces to join the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he reached Jiankang; Prince of Linhe Zhengde led his forces to join the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊午朔，設壇，刑白馬，祀蚩尤於太極殿前。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on wuwu, the first day of the month, an altar was set up; a white horse was sacrificed; Chiyou was sacrificed to before the Hall of Supreme Polarity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuwu, the first day of the month, an altar was set up, a white horse was sacrificed, and Chiyou was worshipped before the Hall of Supreme Polarity.

sentences.zh: 己未，景立蕭正德為天子于南闕前。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Jing established Xiao Zhengde as Son of Heaven before the southern gate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Jing established Xiao Zhengde as Son of Heaven before the southern gate.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，賊攻陷東府城。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the rebels attacked and captured the Eastern Palace city.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the rebels attacked and captured the Eastern Palace city.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，邵陵王綸帥武州刺史蕭弄璋、前譙州刺史趙伯超等入援。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Prince of Shaoling Lun led Xiao Nongzhang, Governor of Wu Province, Zhao Bochao, former Governor of Qiao Province, and others in relief.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Prince of Shaoling Lun led Xiao Nongzhang, Governor of Wu Province, Zhao Bochao, former Governor of Qiao Province, and others in relief.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，進軍湖頭，與賊戰，敗績。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the army advanced to Hutou and fought the rebels; it was routed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the army advanced to Hutou and fought the rebels but was routed.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，安北將軍鄱陽王範遣世子嗣、雄信將軍裴之高等率眾入援，次張公洲。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Prince of Poyang Fan dispatched his heir Si, Pei Zhigao, General of Trustworthy Martiality, and others to lead forces in relief, halting at Zhanggong Isle.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Prince of Poyang Fan dispatched his heir Si, Pei Zhigao, General of Trustworthy Martiality, and others to lead forces in relief, halting at Zhanggong Isle.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊申，天西北裂，有光如火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on wushen, the sky split in the northwest; there was light like fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wushen, the sky split in the northwest with light like fire.

sentences.zh: 尚書令謝舉卒。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Xie Ju died.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Xie Ju died.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，司州刺史柳仲禮、前衡州刺史韋粲、高州刺史李遷仕、前司州刺史羊鴉仁等率軍入援。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Liu Zhongli, Governor of Si Province, Wei Can, former Governor of Heng Province, Li Qianshi, Governor of Gao Province, Yang Yaren, former Governor of Si Province, and others led armies in relief.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Liu Zhongli, Governor of Si Province, Wei Can, former Governor of Heng Province, Li Qianshi, Governor of Gao Province, Yang Yaren, former Governor of Si Province, and others led armies in relief.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丁巳，大都督柳仲禮率眾軍分據南岸，賊濟軍於青塘，襲殺韋粲。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year on dingsi, Commander-in-Chief Liu Zhongli led the armies to hold the south bank; the rebels crossed the army at Qingtang and in a raid killed Wei Can.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the third year, on dingsi, Commander-in-Chief Liu Zhongli led the armies to hold the south bank; the rebels crossed at Qingtang and in a raid killed Wei Can.

sentences.zh: 庚申，白虹貫日三重。

translations.literal: On gengshen, a white rainbow pierced the sun threefold.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen a white rainbow pierced the sun threefold.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸、臨城公大連等率兵集南岸。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun, Duke of Lincheng Dalian, and others gathered troops on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shaoling Lun, Duke of Lincheng Dalian, and others gathered troops on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，有流星長三十丈，墮武庫。

translations.literal: On wuchen, a meteor thirty zhang long fell on the armory.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen a meteor thirty zhang long fell on the armory.

sentences.zh: 李遷仕及天門太守樊文皎進軍青溪東，為賊所破，文皎死之。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi and Fan Wenjiao, Administrator of Tianmen, advanced east of Qingxi and were broken by the rebels; Wenjiao died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi and Fan Wenjiao, Administrator of Tianmen, advanced east of Qingxi and were broken by the rebels; Wenjiao died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 壬午，熒惑守心。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Spark Star guarded the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Spark Star guarded the Heart.

sentences.zh: 二月，侯景遣使求和，皇太子固請，帝乃許之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Hou Jing sent envoys seeking peace; the Crown Prince firmly requested it; the Emperor then assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Hou Jing sent envoys seeking peace; the Crown Prince firmly requested it and the Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 盟于西華門下。

translations.literal: They swore alliance below the West Splendor Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They swore alliance below the West Splendor Gate.

sentences.zh: 景既運東城米歸於石頭，亦不解圍，啟求遣諸軍退。

translations.literal: After Jing transported the Eastern Palace grain to Shitou, he still did not lift the siege; he memorialized requesting that the armies withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing transported the Eastern Palace grain to Shitou he still did not lift the siege and memorialized requesting that the armies withdraw.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇太子又命南兗州刺史南康王會理、前青冀二州刺史湘潭侯退率江北之眾，頓于蘭亭苑。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Crown Prince again ordered Prince of Nankang Huili, former Governor of the two provinces of Qing and Ji, and Duke of Xiangtan Tui to lead the forces north of the river, encamping at Lanting Park.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the Crown Prince again ordered Prince of Nankang Huili, former Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, and Duke of Xiangtan Tui to lead the forces north of the river, encamping at Lanting Park.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以開府儀同三司、丹陽尹邵陵王綸為司空，以合州刺史鄱陽王範為征北大將軍、開府儀同三司，以司州刺史柳仲禮為侍中、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Prince of Shaoling Lun, with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies and Governor of Danyang, was made Minister of Works; Prince of Poyang Fan, Governor of He Province, was made General Who Conquers the North with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies; Liu Zhongli, Governor of Si Province, was made Attendant and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Prince of Shaoling Lun, with the insignia of Opening an Office and Peer of the Three Excellencies and Governor of Danyang, was appointed Minister of Works; Prince of Poyang Fan, Governor of He Province, was made General Who Conquers the North with the same insignia; Liu Zhongli, Governor of Si Province, was made Attendant and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時景奸計既成，乃表陳帝失，復舉兵向闕。

translations.literal: At this time Jing's treacherous plan was already complete; he then memorialized listing the Emperor's faults and again raised troops toward the palace.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jing's treacherous plan was complete; he memorialized listing the Emperor's faults and again raised troops toward the palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，城內以景違盟，設壇告天地神祗。

translations.literal: In the third month, within the city because Jing had violated the alliance, an altar was set up to announce to Heaven and Earth and the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, because Jing had violated the alliance, an altar was set up within the city to announce to Heaven, Earth, and the spirits.

sentences.zh: 戊午，前司州刺史羊鴉仁等進軍東府北，與賊戰，大敗。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Yang Yaren and others advanced north of the Eastern Palace and fought the rebels; they were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Yang Yaren and others advanced north of the Eastern Palace and fought the rebels but were greatly defeated.

sentences.zh: 時四方征鎮入援者三十餘萬，莫有鬥志，自相抄奪而已。

translations.literal: At this time the regional commanders and garrisons coming in relief numbered more than three hundred thousand; none had fighting will — they merely plundered one another.
translations.idiomatic: At this time regional commanders and garrisons coming in relief numbered more than three hundred thousand; none had the will to fight — they merely plundered one another.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，賊攻陷宮城，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the rebels attacked and captured the palace city and let the troops plunder greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the rebels attacked and captured the palace city and let the troops plunder freely.

sentences.zh: 己巳，賊矯詔遣石城公大款解外援軍。

translations.literal: On jisi, the rebels forged an edict dispatching Duke of Shicheng Dakuan to disband the external relief armies.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the rebels forged an edict dispatching Duke of Shicheng Dakuan to disband the external relief armies.

sentences.zh: 庚午，侯景自為都督中外諸軍事、大丞相、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Hou Jing himself became Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Chancellor, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Hou Jing himself became Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Chancellor, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 辛未，援軍各退散。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the relief armies each withdrew and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the relief armies each withdrew and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，熒惑守心。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Spark Star guarded the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the Spark Star guarded the Heart.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己丑，都下地震。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on jichou, the capital shook with an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jichou, the capital was shaken by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 丙申，又震。

translations.literal: On bingshen, it shook again.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen it shook again.

sentences.zh: 己酉，帝以所求不供，憂憤寢疾。

translations.literal: On jiyou, because what was requested was not supplied, the Emperor grieved and fell ill from worry.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, because what was requested was not supplied, the Emperor grieved and fell ill from worry.

sentences.zh: 是月，青冀二州刺史明少遐、東徐州刺史湛海珍、北青州刺史王奉伯各舉州附東魏。

translations.literal: This month, Ming Shaoxia, Governor of the two provinces of Qing and Ji, Zhan Haizhen, Governor of Eastern Xu Province, and Wang Fengbo, Governor of Northern Qing Province, each submitted their province to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That month Ming Shaoxia, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, Zhan Haizhen, Governor of Eastern Xu Province, and Wang Fengbo, Governor of Northern Qing Province, each submitted their province to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 五月丙辰，帝崩于淨居殿，時年八十六。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on bingchen, the Emperor died in the Pure Dwelling Hall; he was then eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingchen, the Emperor died in the Pure Dwelling Hall; he was eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，遷梓宮於太極前殿。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the coffin was moved to the Hall of Supreme Polarity.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the coffin was moved to the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Polarity.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，葬于修陵，追尊為武皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on yimao, he was buried at Xiuling; posthumously honored as Emperor Wu; temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao, he was buried at Xiuling; posthumously honored as Emperor Wu with temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 帝性淳孝，六歲，獻皇太后崩，水漿不入口三日，哭泣有過成人。

translations.literal: The Emperor's nature was pure filial piety; at six sui the Empress Dowager Xian died; for three days he took neither water nor broth; his weeping exceeded that of adults.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's nature was pure filial piety. At six sui the Empress Dowager Xian died; for three days he took neither water nor broth, and his weeping exceeded that of adults.

sentences.zh: 及丁文帝憂，時為齊隨王諮議，隨府在荊鎮，以病聞，便投劾星馳，不復寢食，倍道就路。

translations.literal: When he completed mourning for Emperor Wen, he was then Adviser under the Prince of Sui of Qi; the princely establishment was at Jing garrison; on hearing of the illness he at once submitted his resignation and galloped by starlight; he no longer slept or ate, doubling the road's pace.
translations.idiomatic: When he completed mourning for Emperor Wen he was Adviser under the Prince of Sui of Qi, whose establishment was at Jing garrison; on hearing of the illness he submitted his resignation and galloped by starlight, neither sleeping nor eating, pressing double pace on the road.

sentences.zh: 憤風驚浪，不暫停止。

translations.literal: Furious winds and alarming waves — he did not pause briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Through furious winds and alarming waves he did not pause.

sentences.zh: 帝形容本壯，及至都，銷毀骨立，親表士友，皆不復識。

translations.literal: The Emperor's form was originally robust; when he reached the capital he wasted until only bones stood; relatives, friends, and scholars all no longer recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's form was originally robust; when he reached the capital he had wasted to skin and bone, and relatives, friends, and scholars no longer recognized him.

sentences.zh: 望宅奉諱，氣絕久之。

translations.literal: Gazing at the residence on receiving the tabooed name, his breath ceased for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the residence on receiving the tabooed name, his breath ceased for a long time.

sentences.zh: 每哭，輒歐血數升。

translations.literal: Each time he wept he vomited blood several sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he wept he vomited several sheng of blood.

sentences.zh: 服內，日惟食麥二溢。

translations.literal: Within the mourning period, each day he ate only two yi of wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the mourning period he ate only two yi of wheat each day.

sentences.zh: 拜掃山陵，涕淚所灑，松草變色。

translations.literal: When he bowed and swept the mountain tombs, wherever his tears fell the pines and grass changed color.
translations.idiomatic: When he bowed and swept the mountain tombs, wherever his tears fell the pines and grass changed color.

sentences.zh: 及居帝位，即於鍾山造大愛敬寺，青溪邊造智度寺，於台內立至敬等殿，又立七廟堂。

translations.literal: When he took the imperial throne, he at once at Zhongshan built the Great Temple of Loving Reverence; by the Qing Stream built the Temple of Wisdom; within the palace established the Hall of Utmost Reverence and others; also established the Hall of the Seven Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the imperial throne he at once built the Great Temple of Loving Reverence at Zhongshan and the Temple of Wisdom by the Qing Stream; within the palace he established the Hall of Utmost Reverence and the Hall of the Seven Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 月中再設淨饌，每至展拜，涕泗滂沱，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Twice each month he set out pure offerings; each time he performed the bowing rites, tears streamed in torrents, moving those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Twice each month he set out pure offerings; each time he performed the bowing rites tears streamed in torrents, moving those at his side.

sentences.zh: 少而篤學，能事畢究，雖萬機多務，猶卷不輟手，然燭側光，常至戊夜。

translations.literal: From youth he was deeply devoted to learning and could bring affairs to thorough completion; though the myriad tasks were many, still his hand did not cease turning pages; beside the candle's side light, often until the fifth watch of night.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was deeply devoted to learning and brought affairs to thorough completion; though myriad tasks pressed upon him his hand did not cease turning pages, often by candlelight until the fifth watch.

sentences.zh: 撰通史六百卷，金海三十卷，制旨孝經義、周易講疏及六十四卦、二系、文言、序卦等義，樂社義、毛詩、春秋答問、尚書大義、中庸講疏、孔子正言、孝經講疏，凡二百餘卷。

translations.literal: He compiled the Comprehensive History in six hundred fascicles, Golden Sea in thirty fascicles, imperially composed Filial Piety Classic Exegesis, Zhou Changes Lecture Commentary and the commentaries on the sixty-four hexagrams, the two commentaries, the Wenyan, the Sequence of Hexagrams, and others, Music and Community Exegesis, Mao Odes, Spring and Autumn Question-and-Answer, Great Meaning of the Documents, Doctrine of the Mean Lecture Commentary, Confucius's Correct Words, Filial Piety Lecture Commentary — in all more than two hundred fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the Comprehensive History in six hundred fascicles and Golden Sea in thirty fascicles; he composed imperial exegeses on the Filial Piety Classic, lecture commentaries on the Zhou Changes and its sixty-four hexagrams, the two commentaries, the Wenyan, and the Sequence of Hexagrams; Music and Community Exegesis, the Mao Odes, Spring and Autumn Question-and-Answer, Great Meaning of the Documents, Doctrine of the Mean Lecture Commentary, Confucius's Correct Words, and Filial Piety Lecture Commentary — more than two hundred fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 王侯朝臣皆奉表質疑，帝皆為解釋。

translations.literal: Princes, marquises, and court ministers all submitted memorials raising questions; the Emperor all explained them.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, marquises, and court ministers all submitted memorials raising questions, and the Emperor answered each one.

sentences.zh: 修飾國學，增廣生員，立五館，置五經博士。

translations.literal: He renovated the Imperial Academy, increased the student quota, established the Five Halls, and appointed doctors of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He renovated the Imperial Academy, increased the student quota, established the Five Halls, and appointed doctors of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 天監初，何佟之、賀瑒、嚴植之、明山賓等覆述制旨，並撰吉凶賓軍嘉五禮，一千餘卷，帝稱制斷疑焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, He Tongzhi, He Chang, Yan Zhizhi, Ming Shanbin, and others reviewed the imperial compositions and together compiled the five rites of auspicious, inauspicious, guest, military, and celebratory — more than one thousand fascicles; the Emperor said he decided doubtful points.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian, He Tongzhi, He Chang, Yan Zhizhi, Ming Shanbin, and others reviewed the imperial compositions and together compiled the five rites of auspicious, inauspicious, guest, military, and celebratory rites — more than one thousand fascicles; the Emperor said he decided doubtful points.

sentences.zh: 大同中，於台西立士林館，領軍朱異、太府卿賀琛、舍人孔子驅等遞互講述。

translations.literal: In Datong, west of the palace the Forest of Scholars Hall was established; Army Supervisor Zhu Yi, Grand Steward He Chen, Attendant Kongzi Qu, and others lectured in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era the Forest of Scholars Hall was established west of the palace; Army Supervisor Zhu Yi, Grand Steward He Chen, Attendant Kongzi Qu, and others lectured in rotation.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、宣城王亦于東宮宣猷堂及揚州廨開講。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince and Prince of Xuancheng also opened lectures at the Propagation of Virtue Hall in the Eastern Palace and at the Yangzhou yamen.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince and Prince of Xuancheng also opened lectures at the Propagation of Virtue Hall in the Eastern Palace and at the Yangzhou yamen.

sentences.zh: 於是四方郡國，莫不向風。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the four directions, commanderies and states, none failed to turn toward the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon throughout the realm commanderies and states turned toward the court's influence.

sentences.zh: 爰自在田，及登寶位，躬制贊、序、詔誥、銘、誄、說、箴、頌、箋、奏諸文，又百二十卷。

translations.literal: From the time he was in the fields until he ascended the precious throne, he personally composed prefaces, introductions, edicts, proclamations, inscriptions, dirges, disquisitions, admonitions, eulogies, letters, and memorials — again one hundred twenty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he was in the fields until he ascended the throne he personally composed prefaces, introductions, edicts, proclamations, inscriptions, dirges, disquisitions, admonitions, eulogies, letters, and memorials — one hundred twenty fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 六藝備閑，棋登逸品，陰陽、緯候、卜筮、占決、草隸、尺牘、騎射，莫不稱妙。

translations.literal: The Six Arts he fully mastered; at chess he reached transcendent rank; yin-yang, weft texts, divination, prognostication, clerical and cursive script, letters, horsemanship, and archery — none failed to be called marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: He fully mastered the Six Arts; at chess he reached transcendent rank; yin-yang, weft texts, divination, prognostication, clerical and cursive script, letters, horsemanship, and archery — in none did he fail to excel.

sentences.zh: 晚乃溺信佛道，日止一食，膳無鮮腴，惟豆羹糲飯而已。

translations.literal: In his later years he drowned in faith in the Buddhist Way; each day only one meal; in provisions no fresh or rich foods — only bean broth and coarse rice.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he drowned in Buddhist faith; he ate only one meal a day, with no fresh or rich foods — only bean broth and coarse rice.

sentences.zh: 或遇事擁，日儻移中，便嗽口以過。

translations.literal: Or when affairs pressed, if the day passed midday he merely rinsed his mouth and passed on.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs pressed and the day passed midday he merely rinsed his mouth and went on.

sentences.zh: 制涅盤、大品、淨名、三慧諸經義記數百卷。

translations.literal: He composed exegeses and lecture records on the Nirvana, Great Perfection, Vimalakirti, Three Wisdom, and other sutras — several hundred fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He composed exegeses and lecture records on the Nirvana, Great Perfection, Vimalakirti, Three Wisdom, and other sutras — several hundred fascicles.

sentences.zh: 聽覽餘閒，即於重雲殿及同泰寺講說，名僧碩學，四部聽眾，常萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the spare time after audience, then at the Chongyun Hall and Tongtai Temple he lectured; famous monks and great scholars; the fourfold audience often numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In spare time after audience he lectured at the Chongyun Hall and Tongtai Temple; famous monks and great scholars and a fourfold audience often numbered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 身衣布衣，木綿皁帳，一冠三載，一被二年。

translations.literal: He personally wore cloth robes, cotton and black canopy; one cap for three years, one quilt for two years.
translations.idiomatic: He personally wore cloth robes and cotton bedding with a black canopy; one cap lasted three years, one quilt two years.

sentences.zh: 自五十外便斷房室，後宮職司貴妃以下，六宮褘褕三翟之外，皆衣不曳地，傍無錦綺。

translations.literal: From after fifty he cut off the bedchamber entirely; in the inner palace, officials and consorts below Noble Consort — apart from the six palaces' ceremonial robes and the three pheasant patterns — all wore garments not trailing on the ground, with no brocade or damask at the sides.
translations.idiomatic: From after fifty he cut off the bedchamber entirely; in the inner palace, officials and consorts below Noble Consort — apart from the six palaces' ceremonial robes and the three pheasant patterns — all wore garments that did not trail on the ground, with no brocade or damask at the sides.

sentences.zh: 不飲酒，不聽音聲，非宗廟祭祀、大會饗宴及諸法事，未嘗作樂。

translations.literal: He did not drink wine, did not listen to music; except for ancestral temple sacrifice, great assemblies and feasts, and various dharma affairs, he never made music.
translations.idiomatic: He did not drink wine or listen to music; except for ancestral temple sacrifice, great assemblies and feasts, and various dharma affairs, he never had music performed.

sentences.zh: 勤於政務，孜孜無怠。

translations.literal: He was diligent in government affairs, tireless and unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in government affairs, tireless and unceasing.

sentences.zh: 每冬月四更竟，即敕把燭看事，執筆觸寒，手為皴裂。

translations.literal: Each winter month when the fourth watch ended, he at once ordered candles brought to review affairs; holding the brush in the cold, his hands cracked with chilblains.
translations.idiomatic: Each winter when the fourth watch ended he ordered candles brought to review affairs; holding the brush in the cold his hands cracked with chilblains.

sentences.zh: 然仁愛不斷，親親及所愛愆犯多有縱舍，故政刑弛紊。

translations.literal: Yet his benevolence was indecisive; among kin and those he loved, many offenses were often pardoned — therefore government and punishments grew lax and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his benevolence was indecisive; among kin and those he loved many offenses were pardoned — and government and punishments grew lax and disordered.

sentences.zh: 每決死罪，常有哀矜涕泣，然後可奏。

translations.literal: Each time he decided a capital crime, there were always pity and tears before it could be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he decided a capital case he wept with pity before it could be submitted.

sentences.zh: 性方正，雖居小殿暗室，恒理衣冠小坐，暑月未嘗褰袒。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and square; though he dwelt in a small hall or dark room, he always arranged cap and robes for a small sitting; in summer months he never bared his shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was upright; though he dwelt in a small hall or dark room he always arranged cap and robes properly; in summer he never bared his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 雖見內豎小臣，亦如遇大賓也。

translations.literal: Though he saw inner attendants or minor servants, he treated them as if meeting a great guest.
translations.idiomatic: Though he saw inner attendants or minor servants he treated them as if meeting a great guest.

sentences.zh: 初，齊高帝夢屐而登殿，顧見武、明二帝后一人手張天地圖而不識，問之，答曰：「順子後。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Gao of Qi dreamed he climbed the hall in clogs; looking back he saw the two empresses Wu and Ming — one held open the map of Heaven and Earth and he did not recognize her; he asked, and she answered: "After Shunzi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Gao of Qi dreamed he climbed the hall in clogs; looking back he saw the two empresses Wu and Ming — one held open the map of Heaven and Earth and he did not recognize her; he asked, and she answered: "After Shunzi.

sentences.zh: 」及崔慧景之逼，長沙宣武王入援，至越城，夢乘馬飛半天而墜，帝所馭化為赤龍，騰虛獨上。

translations.literal: " When Cui Huijing pressed close, Prince of Changsha Xuanwu entered in relief; reaching Yuecheng, he dreamed he rode a horse flying half into the sky then falling; the steed the Emperor rode transformed into a red dragon and soared alone upward.
translations.idiomatic: "When Cui Huijing pressed close, Prince of Changsha Xuanwu entered in relief; reaching Yuecheng he dreamed he rode a horse flying halfway into the sky then falling; the steed the Emperor rode transformed into a red dragon and soared alone upward.

sentences.zh: 時台內有宿衛士為覡，常見太極殿有六龍各守一柱，末忽失其二，後見在宣武王宅。

translations.literal: At that time within the palace there was a guard who was a diviner; he often saw six dragons each guarding one pillar of the Hall of Supreme Polarity; suddenly two at the end were lost; afterward he saw them at Prince of Xuanwu's residence.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a guard within the palace who was a diviner often saw six dragons each guarding one pillar of the Hall of Supreme Polarity; suddenly two vanished, and later he saw them at Prince of Xuanwu's residence.

sentences.zh: 時宣武為益州，覡乃往蜀伏事。

translations.literal: At that time Xuanwu was in Yizhou; the diviner then went to Shu to serve in secret.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuanwu was in Yizhou; the diviner went to Shu to serve in secret.

sentences.zh: 及宣武在郢，此覡還都，乃見六龍俱在帝所寢齋，遂去郢之雍。

translations.literal: When Xuanwu was at Ying, this diviner returned to the capital; then he saw all six dragons together at the Emperor's sleeping quarters; thereupon he left Ying for Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanwu was at Ying this diviner returned to the capital and saw all six dragons together at the Emperor's sleeping quarters; thereupon he left Ying for Yong.

sentences.zh: 中途遇疾且死，謂同侶曰：「蕭雍州必作天子。

translations.literal: Midway he met illness and was near death; he told his companions: "Governor Xiao of Yong Province will surely become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Midway he fell ill near death and told his companions: "Governor Xiao of Yong Province will surely become Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」具以前事語之。

translations.literal: " He fully told them the earlier affair.
translations.idiomatic: "He fully told them the earlier affair.

sentences.zh: 推此而言，蓋天命也。

translations.literal: Pushing this to speak, probably it was Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing this to speak, it was probably Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 雖在蒙塵，齋戒不廢，及疾不能進膳，盥漱如初。

translations.literal: Though in dust and hardship, he did not cease fasting and purification; when ill and unable to take food, washing and rinsing were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Though in dust and hardship he did not cease fasting and purification; when ill and unable to take food his washing and rinsing were as before.

sentences.zh: 皇太子日中再朝，每問安否，涕泗交面。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince twice each day at noon attended court; each time he asked after his health; tears crossed his face.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince twice each day at noon attended court; each time he asked after his health tears crossed his face.

sentences.zh: 賊臣侍者，莫不掩泣。

translations.literal: The rebel ministers' attendants — none failed to cover their faces and weep.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel ministers' attendants — none failed to cover their faces and weep.

sentences.zh: 疾久口苦，索蜜不得，再曰：「荷，荷！

translations.literal: After long illness his mouth was bitter; he sought honey and did not obtain it; again he said: "He, he!
translations.idiomatic: After long illness his mouth was bitter; he sought honey and could not obtain it; again he said: "He, he!

sentences.zh: 」遂崩。

translations.literal: " Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: "Then he died.

sentences.zh: 賊秘之，太子問起居不得見，慟於合下。

translations.literal: The rebels kept it secret; the Crown Prince asked after his health and could not see him; he grieved below the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels kept it secret; the Crown Prince asked after his health and could not see him, and grieved below the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 始天監中，沙門釋寶志為詩曰：「昔年三十八，今年八十三，四中復有四，城北火酣酣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, the monk Shibao Zhi composed a verse: "In years past thirty-eight, this year eighty-three; within four again four, north of the city fire blazes blazes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian the monk Shibao Zhi composed a verse: "In years past thirty-eight, this year eighty-three; within four again four, north of the city fire blazes blazes.

sentences.zh: 」帝使周舍封記之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor had Zhou She seal and record it.
translations.idiomatic: "The Emperor had Zhou She seal and record it.

sentences.zh: 及中大同元年，同泰寺災，帝啟封見舍手跡，為之流涕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong, Tongtai Temple was destroyed by fire; the Emperor opened the seal and saw She's own hand; he wept for it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongdatong Tongtai Temple was destroyed by fire; the Emperor opened the seal and saw She's own handwriting and wept.

sentences.zh: 帝生於甲辰，三十八，克建鄴之年也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was born in jiachen; thirty-eight — the year Jiankang was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was born in jiachen; thirty-eight was the year Jiankang was taken.

sentences.zh: 遇災歲實丙寅，八十三矣。

translations.literal: The year of the disaster was truly bingyin; eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The year of the disaster was truly bingyin — eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 四月十四日而火，火起之始，自浮屠第三層。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the fourth month came fire; fire's beginning started from the third story of the pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the fourth month came fire; the fire began from the third story of the pagoda.

sentences.zh: 三者，帝之昆季次也。

translations.literal: Three — the Emperor's brothers' order among siblings.
translations.idiomatic: Three — the Emperor's order among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，召太史令虞履筮之，遇？

translations.literal: The Emperor hated it; he summoned Grand Astrologer Yu Li to divinate; he encountered ?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hated it; he summoned Grand Astrologer Yu Li to divinate and encountered the hexagram Kun.

sentences.zh: 履曰：「無害。

translations.literal: Li said: "No harm.
translations.idiomatic: Li said: "No harm.

sentences.zh: 其繇云：'西南得朋，東北喪朋，安貞吉。

translations.literal: Its line text says: 'In the southwest one finds companions; in the northeast one loses companions; steadfast correctness is auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Its line text says: "In the southwest one finds companions; in the northeast one loses companions; steadfast correctness is auspicious.

sentences.zh: '文言云：'東北喪朋，乃終有慶。

translations.literal: ' The Wenyan says: 'In the northeast one loses companions; in the end there is celebration.
translations.idiomatic: "The Wenyan says: "In the northeast one loses companions; in the end there is celebration.

sentences.zh: '」帝曰：「斯魔鬼也。

translations.literal: ' " The Emperor said: "This is a demon ghost.
translations.idiomatic: "The Emperor said: "This is a demon ghost.

sentences.zh: 酉應見卯，金來克木，卯為陰賊。

translations.literal: You corresponds to mao; metal comes to overcome wood; mao is the yin thief.
translations.idiomatic: You corresponds to mao; metal comes to overcome wood; mao is the yin thief.

sentences.zh: 鬼而帶賊，非魔何也。

translations.literal: Ghost yet bearing thief — if not a demon, what?
translations.idiomatic: A ghost yet bearing thief — if not a demon, what?

sentences.zh: 孰為致之？

translations.literal: Who brought it about?
translations.idiomatic: Who brought it about?

sentences.zh: 酉為口舌，當乎說位。

translations.literal: You is the mouth and tongue; it should correspond to the Speaking position.
translations.idiomatic: You is the mouth and tongue; it should correspond to the Speaking position.

sentences.zh: 說言乎兌，故知善言之口，宜前為法事。

translations.literal: Speaking words belong to Dui; therefore one knows the mouth of good speech should beforehand become a dharma affair.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking words belong to Dui; therefore one knows the mouth of good speech should beforehand become a dharma affair.

sentences.zh: 」於是人人贊善，莫不從風。

translations.literal: Thereupon every person praised goodness; none failed to follow the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every person praised goodness; none failed to follow the wind.

sentences.zh: 或刺血灑地，或刺血書經，穿心然燈，坐禪不食。

translations.literal: Some pricked blood to sprinkle the ground; some pricked blood to write sutras; pierced the heart to burn lamps; sat in meditation without eating.
translations.idiomatic: Some pricked blood to sprinkle the ground; some pricked blood to write sutras; pierced the heart to burn lamps; sat in meditation without eating.

sentences.zh: 及太清元年，帝捨身光嚴、重雲殿，遊仙化生皆震動，三日乃止。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, the Emperor offered his body at the Hall of Radiant Solemnity and Chongyun Hall; Youxian and Huasheng all shook; for three days before it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing the Emperor offered his body at the Hall of Radiant Solemnity and Chongyun Hall; Youxian and Huasheng all shook for three days before stopping.

sentences.zh: 當時謂之祥瑞。

translations.literal: At the time it was called an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was called an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 識者以非動而動，在鴻範為祅。

translations.literal: Those who understood considered that not moving yet moving — in the Great Plan it is portent.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood considered that not moving yet moving — in the Great Plan it is portent.

sentences.zh: 以比石季龍之敗，殿壁畫人頸皆縮入頭之類。

translations.literal: It may be compared to Shi Le's defeat — when the painted people on the hall walls all shrank their necks into their heads, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: It may be compared to Shi Le's defeat — when the painted people on the hall walls all shrank their necks into their heads, and the like.

sentences.zh: 時海中浮鵠山，去余姚岸可千餘里，上有女人年三百歲，有女官道士四五百人，年並出百，但在山學道。

translations.literal: At that time on the sea floated Goose Mountain, more than a thousand li from the shore of Yuyao; on it was a woman three hundred sui old, with four or five hundred female officials and Daoist nuns, all also over a hundred — but all on the mountain studying the Way.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Goose Mountain floated on the sea more than a thousand li from the shore of Yuyao; on it was a woman three hundred sui old, with four or five hundred female officials and Daoist nuns all also over a hundred — all on the mountain studying the Way.

sentences.zh: 遣使獻紅席。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent presenting red mats.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent presenting red mats.

sentences.zh: 帝方捨身時，其使適至，雲此草常有紅鳥居下，故以為名。

translations.literal: The Emperor was just then offering his body; the envoys happened to arrive; they said this grass always had red birds dwelling beneath — therefore it was so named.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was just then offering his body when the envoys arrived; they said this grass always had red birds dwelling beneath — therefore it was so named.

sentences.zh: 觀其圖狀，則鸞鳥也。

translations.literal: Looking at its pictured form, it was the luan bird.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at its pictured form, it was the luan bird.

sentences.zh: 時有男子不知何許人，於大眾中自割身以飴饑鳥，血流遍體，而顏色不變。

translations.literal: At that time there was a man who knew not from what place; in the great assembly he cut his own body to feed hungry birds; blood flowed over his body yet his complexion did not change.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a man of unknown origin who in the great assembly cut his own body to feed hungry birds; blood flowed over his body yet his complexion did not change.

sentences.zh: 又沙門智泉鐵鉤掛體，以然千燈，一日一夜，端坐不動。

translations.literal: Also the monk Zhi Quan hung his body on an iron hook and lit a thousand lamps; for one day and one night he sat upright without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Also the monk Zhi Quan hung his body on an iron hook and lit a thousand lamps; for one day and one night he sat upright without moving.

sentences.zh: 開講日，有三足鳥集殿之東戶，自戶適於西南縣楣，三飛三集。

translations.literal: On the day the lecture opened, a three-footed bird settled on the hall's east door; from the door it went to the southwest ridgepole; three flights and three settlements.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the lecture opened a three-footed bird settled on the hall's east door, then went to the southwest ridgepole — three flights and three settlements.

sentences.zh: 白雀一，見於重雲閣前連理樹。

translations.literal: One white sparrow appeared before the joined tree before the Chongyun Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: A white sparrow appeared before the joined tree before the Chongyun Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又有五色雲浮于華林園昆明池上。

translations.literal: Also five-colored clouds floated above the Kunming Pond in the Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Also five-colored clouds floated above the Kunming Pond in the Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 帝既流遁益甚，境內化之，遂至喪亡云。

translations.literal: The Emperor's wandering in hardship grew ever worse; within the realm they were transformed by it — thus reaching ruin and death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's wandering in hardship grew ever worse; the realm was transformed by it — and thus reached ruin and death.

sentences.zh: 論曰：梁武帝時逢昏虐，家遭冤禍，既地居勢勝，乘機而作，以斯文德，有此武功。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Under Emperor Wu of Liang the times encountered tyranny; the family suffered wrongful calamity; having the terrain and momentum's advantage, he took the opportunity to act; with such civil virtue, he had such martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Under Emperor Wu of Liang the times encountered tyranny and the family suffered wrongful calamity; possessing terrain and momentum he seized the opportunity to act; with such civil virtue he achieved such martial success.

sentences.zh: 始用湯、武之師，終濟唐、虞之業，豈曰人謀，亦惟天命。

translations.literal: At first he used the armies of Tang and Wu; in the end he completed the enterprise of Tang and Yu — can one call it human planning alone? It was also Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: At first he used the armies of Tang and Wu; in the end he completed the enterprise of Tang and Yu — can one call it human planning alone? It was also Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 及據圖籙，多曆歲年，製造禮樂，敦崇儒雅，自江左以來，年踰二百，文物之盛，獨美於茲。

translations.literal: When he held the chart and seal, many years passed; he fashioned rites and music and honored the Confucian and elegant — since east of the river, years exceeding two hundred, in cultural brilliance none surpassed this age.
translations.idiomatic: When he held the chart and seal many years passed; he fashioned rites and music and honored the Confucian and elegant — since east of the river, in more than two hundred years, in cultural brilliance none surpassed this age.

sentences.zh: 然先王文武遞用，德刑備舉，方之水火，取法陰陽，為國之道，不可獨任；

translations.literal: Yet the former kings used civil and martial in alternation; virtue and punishments were both employed; comparing them to water and fire, taking law from yin and yang — the way of governing a state cannot rely on one alone;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the former kings used civil and martial in alternation and employed both virtue and punishments; comparing them to water and fire and taking law from yin and yang — the way of governing a state cannot rely on one alone;

sentences.zh: 而帝留心俎豆，忘情幹戚，溺於釋教，弛于刑典。

translations.literal: while the Emperor fixed his heart on the sacrificial vessels, forgot feeling for the shield and axe, drowned in the Buddhist teaching, and relaxed in the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: while the Emperor fixed his heart on the sacrificial vessels, forgot feeling for shield and axe, drowned in the Buddhist teaching, and relaxed the penal code.

sentences.zh: 既而帝紀不立，悖逆萌生，反噬彎弧，皆自子弟，履霜弗戒，卒至亂亡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial discipline was not established; rebellious thoughts sprouted; turning back to bite and bending the bow — all from his own sons and younger brothers; treading frost without caution, in the end reaching disorder and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon imperial discipline was not established; rebellious thoughts sprouted; turning back to bite and bending the bow — all from his own sons and younger brothers; treading frost without caution, in the end reaching disorder and ruin.

sentences.zh: 自古撥亂之君，固已多矣，其或樹置失所，而以後嗣失之，未有自己而得，自己而喪。

translations.literal: Since ancient times, lords who raised order have indeed been many; those who erred in establishing heirs and through later successors lost the realm — none obtained it by themselves and lost it by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times lords who raised order have indeed been many; those who erred in establishing heirs and lost the realm through later successors — none obtained it by themselves and lost it by themselves.

sentences.zh: 追蹤徐偃之仁，以致窮門之酷，可為深痛，可為至戒者乎！

translations.literal: Pursuing the benevolence of Xu Yan and thereby reaching the cruelty of the impoverished gate — can this not be deeply painful, can this not be the utmost warning!
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the benevolence of Xu Yan and thereby reaching the cruelty of the impoverished gate — can this not be deeply painful? Can this not be the utmost warning!
